ratings_why.fun: Clear growth shape: Stamps and Landlady passes early, Spawn decisions mid-game, Alder and Bradán bursts late, and each Spawn is a real cost-or-reward call.
ratings_why.distinct: The swap river with bank folk sliding down as obstacles is fresh, but Spawn coming home with stats kept sits close to Birds' Fly South.

verdict_why: One real unclear rule (Mother Redd copies into a full hand) is worth a line; the rest plays well as it stands.

points.text: Say what happens to Mother Redd's copies when the hand is full: do they wait like a returning fish, or are they lost? With Old Kelt laps she can make several a turn.

Old Kelt with Mother Redd means a fish stays on board and still sends a copy each lap, so they stop being two different answers. Consider whether Kelt's kept Spawns should skip Redd, or leave it as the high roll.
Thumbprint Parr takes six fights to fill on its own Leap, so its Spawn rarely lands before Tier 4. A first-turn Stamp or a bigger Spawn would let the seed pay off on curve.
Ghillie Stoat's once-a-turn gold is thin next to the Landlady; letting it trigger in fights too (paid next turn) would make it a pick in leap boards.
Early turns lean on Brother Grilse and the Hen to make any Leaps at all; a second cheap Start of Combat Leap at Tier 2 would smooth the first three turns.

standouts.why: The Landlady catching a whole Kype column one fish after another is the tribe's best early moment.
The Bear turns Spawn from a wait into a choice and grows himself, a strong mid-game pivot.
The Alder is a stable carry that never leaves, giving the spending fish a place their power lands.

weakest.why: About 1 gold a turn with a narrow trigger; you take the Landlady instead.
Grows slowly and its Spawn is small for how long it takes to arrive.
Big in-fight numbers but only once the front row dies, and nothing permanent.

flags.note: With The Salmon of Llyn Llyw and Weir-Jumper, Fry deaths refill a passport mid-fight and each lap leaves three more Fry; only board space and enemy attacks stop it.
With Old Kelt laps, the Alder gains a fish's full stats several times a fight, permanently; could outgrow any Tier 6 target.
Mother Redd with the Bear, or with Kelt laps, can make a triple and a Discover nearly every turn late.
Copies into a full hand are not ruled.
Uncle Faroe with the Bear and Little Jack is 6 gold a turn plus a replayed Leap; worth the owner's eye on economy.
